gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Belkin's own spec table for the 12-outlet BE112230-08 lists 3,780 J of total joules, not the 3,940 J that the same page's description and ChatGPT's answer use, or that its clamping voltage is 400 V only line-to-neutral and 500 V on the line-to-ground and neutral-to-ground modes.
standout_why: I compared against honestfred.com (rank 2/4, read 2026-11-08). It gives joules for one product only (Anker 351, 2,100 J), no clamping voltage or VPR for any pick, and no end-of-life behaviour beyond the advice to look for an indicator light. I could not read the two cited rivals: tomsguide.com came back with only its title, and goodhousekeeping.com plus its Yahoo copy refused the fetch (blocked and 403). So I can't rule out that Tom's Guide or Good Housekeeping prints clamping voltages. The score is held at 1 for that reason; if neither does, it would be a 2.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Both Belkin strips state on their US product pages that they cut power when protection is spent ('Power Safety Shut Down: Yes'). The joule headline is not a fair comparison number: the BE112230-08 page gives two totals (3,780 J and 3,940 J), and its 400 V clamping figure covers only one of three modes. Between the two Belkins, the PivotPlug BP112230-08 is the cleaner spec at 4,320 J with a single 400 V clamping figure ($49.99), and the BE112230-08 is cheaper ($30.99). Both are out of stock at belkin.com today. I could not source the Anker 2100J, the CyberPower or the Tripp Lite strips from their makers' pages (see unsourced), so the table can only show the Belkin rows.
